Root Cause Analysis — 6 issues
Reviews → Negative Handling 2.0
No negative or critical reviews are present in this sample. The repeated '3 months consistency' messaging in reviews [3] and [5] suggests preemptive objection handling but zero actual negative feedback is visible.
Surface 2-3 genuine 3-4 star reviews that mention common objections (taste, price, waiting for results) with visible brand responses demonstrating empathy and solutions. Example response template: 'Hi [Name], we understand 3 months feels long—here's why consistency matters for cellular energy [link]. We're here if you need support.' This converts skepticism into confidence.
Visual Design → Before / After 2.0
Zero before/after transformation visual on entire PDP. The only comparison (howWeCompareV2) shows product format checkmarks (gummies vs resin), not user outcomes. No visualization of the '3PM crash' elimination or the 'fitness score improvement journey' referenced in the clinical study.
Create a split-screen 'Energy Curve' infographic: Left side shows typical day with crash at 3PM (red zone), right side shows sustained energy line with Shilajit (green zone). Add a '90-Day Journey' timeline showing fitness score progression milestones at Day 30/60/90 based on the placebo-controlled study data. Place above the fold or immediately after hero image.
Visual Design → Lifestyle Shots 2.5
Only contextual shots are: product on windowsill, product being held, and a gym torso. No images showing boardroom confidence, travel scenarios, family moments, or gym-to-work transitions. 'How To Use' illustration uses a generic cartoon silhouette drinking water.
Commission 3 lifestyle shots: (1) Well-groomed 35-40yo professional taking gummy before laptop/meeting setup, (2) Airport lounge context with supplement jar + passport + laptop, (3) Morning routine flat-lay with gym bag + gummy jar + car keys. Replace cartoon 'How To Use' with real photography of consumption in premium environment.
Visual Design → Human Presence 3.5
Only one image (reviews_recursive_1) shows a human figure—a muscular male torso in gym tank top with no face visible. Zero representation of Tejas' actual lifestyle context (business meetings, travel, family). No depiction of mid-day energy crash or recovery moments.
Add hero image of a well-groomed 35-40yo man in business casual (rolled sleeves, quality watch) looking energized at 4PM with gummy jar subtly visible. Include secondary image showing the 'before' state—same demographic looking drained at desk with clock showing 3PM. This creates instant recognition and aspiration.
Ad Alignment → ATC Drop-off Addressed 4.5
ATC rates reach 30.9% but conversion data is N/A, indicating significant post-ATC abandonment. PDP shows: no urgency/scarcity triggers, no daily cost breakdown (₹XX/day), '1 Month Pack' headline creates commitment anxiety, no visible guarantee/refund policy, benefits use technical jargon ('fulvic acid', 'cellular energy production') instead of outcomes.
Add directly above ATC button: 'Just ₹33/day for all-day energy • 100% money-back guarantee if you don't feel the difference in 30 days.' Create a 'Starter Week' option at ₹299 to reduce first-purchase friction. Add micro-copy: '87% of customers reorder within 90 days' to signal low regret rate.
Reviews → Freshness 5.0
All 5 displayed reviews are from 106-117 days ago (late April to early May 2026), placing them approximately 3.5-4 months old. Most recent review is May 10, 2026. No reviews from the last 3 months exist in this sample.
Implement automated post-purchase email sequence: Day 7 (first impressions), Day 30 (early results), Day 90 (transformation review request with photo incentive). Surface reviews with 'Verified Purchase: X days ago' badges. Pin one review from last 30 days at top with 'Most Recent' label to signal active, satisfied customer base.

Rewrite headline to: 'Finally, All-Day Energy That Survives Your 10-to-7' with subhead: 'No prep. No crash. Just 2 gummies after breakfast.' This directly addresses Tejas's work-window energy concern and the convenience pillar.
Carousel Flow
6.0/10
The carousel labels (hero_1 through hero_8) suggest multiple slides but without visible content descriptions, the flow cannot be fully evaluated. However, the body copy does follow a partial narrative arc: it opens with clinical proof ('Clinically Studied | 3rd Party Lab Tested'), moves to solution benefits ('2.5x Higher Absorption'), and addresses convenience ('Most people who try Shilajit resin quit within two weeks... Restructure page to open with: 'The 3 PM wall isn't weakness—it's biology. You're doing everything right: gym, diet, sleep. But somewhere between the morning alarm and the evening commute, your energy account hits zero.' THEN introduce the solution.

3.5/10
Only one image (reviews_recursive_1) shows a human figure - a muscular male torso in a gym tank top, which aligns with the fitness-focused persona. However, there is no face visible, no representation of the 'Tejas' persona's actual lifestyle context (business meetings, travel, family), and no depiction of the mid-day energy crash or recovery moments. The persona is a performance-driven professional experiencing work depletion, yet visuals show only gym context without the boardroom-to-gym duality.
Add 2-3 lifestyle images showing a well-groomed 30-40 year old man in business casual attire experiencing the 3PM slump at a desk, then energized post-gummy. Include a travel context shot (airport lounge, hotel room with supplement) to match his travel-heavy lifestyle. Show the dignity/looking-good-for-age aspiration.
Proof Prominence
7.5/10
Clinical proof is well-represented across multiple dedicated slides (clinicalProof images) with '25% Improvement in Fitness Score' and '23% Reduction in stress level' prominently displayed in large typography around the product. The '2.5x better absorption' claim appears multiple times. Third-party lab testing is shown with actual certificate documents (clinicalProof_recursive_5, 6) and NABL accreditation is mentioned. However, the proof percentages could be larger and the certificates are difficult to read at thumbnail size.
Increase the font size of '25%' and '23%' stats by 30% and add a contrasting colour (gold or green) to make them pop. Create a dedicated 'trust badge' strip with lab logos (Eurofins, Equinox Labs) that's scannable at mobile thumbnail size. The journal publication reference is buried in small footer text - elevate it.
Ingredient Imagery
7.8/10
Ingredients are shown effectively in petri dishes (hero_5, keyIngredients images) creating a clinical/premium aesthetic. Raw Shilajit chunks and KSM-66 Ashwagandha roots are displayed clearly with dosage callouts (300mg, 40mg). The 'Our Trademarked Shilajit Recipe' slide shows all four key ingredients in white dishes against neutral background. However, Black Pepper and Chicory Root from the claims are not visually highlighted despite being mentioned. The green microscopic cell image (hero_3) for absorption is abstract.
Add visual representation of Chicory Root and Black Pepper with their specific benefits (prebiotic fiber GI of 2, piperine for absorption). Replace the abstract green cell imagery with a more intuitive 'absorption pathway' infographic showing ingredients entering the body.
Before / After
2.0/10
There is no before/after transformation visual anywhere in the PDP. The comparison slide (howWeCompareV2) only compares product formats (gummies vs resin) with checkmarks, not user outcomes. For a persona experiencing the '3PM crash' and wanting to 'look good for his age,' there is zero visual representation of the energy/vitality transformation or the fitness score improvement journey.
Create a split-screen 'Day with vs without' energy curve visualization showing the 3PM crash being eliminated. Add a '90-day journey' infographic referencing the placebo-controlled study showing fitness score improvement over time. Consider a subtle 'tired businessman → energized businessman' visual sequence.
Lifestyle Shots
2.5/10
Lifestyle imagery is severely lacking. The only contextual shots are: product on windowsill (reviews_recursive_2), product being held (reviews_recursive_4, 5), and gym torso (reviews_recursive_1). There are no images showing the persona's aspirational life - no boardroom confidence, no travel scenarios, no family moments, no gym-to-work transitions. The 'How To Use' illustration is a generic cartoon silhouette drinking water.
Add a hero lifestyle image showing a sharp-dressed 35-40 year old professional taking gummies before a meeting or during travel. Include a morning routine shot (gym bag + gummy jar + laptop). Replace cartoon illustration with a real photo of someone consuming the gummy in a premium environment.
Visual Hierarchy & Brand

Brand consistency is strong with Man Matters black/white/grey palette maintained throughout. The product jar is the consistent anchor in most slides. Typography hierarchy is clear with headlines in bold sans-serif. However, the hero image (hero_1) leads with 'India's first Shilajit Gummies with fiber' which is a category claim rather than the key benefit (energy/fitness). Root Cause Analysis — 6 issues
Reviews → Negative Handling 2.0
Zero negative or even moderately critical reviews are displayed. No evidence of brand responses to any reviews.
Display 2-3 genuine 3-4 star reviews that mention real concerns (e.g., 'took 2 weeks to feel effects' or 'wish pack was bigger'). Add brand responses within 24-48 hours that address concerns specifically: 'Hi Rahul, thanks for the feedback. Most customers feel peak energy by day 14 as Shilajit builds up. Keep us posted!' This transforms skepticism into trust.
Ad Alignment → ATC Drop-off Addressed 3.5
Top ads hit 25-31% ATC suggesting strong intent, but PDP shows: (1) No urgency or scarcity, (2) No social proof to validate decision, (3) No clear 'why now', (4) No risk reversal (guarantee not prominent), (5) Price objection not handled despite 'price slash' ad performing well.
Add above-the-fold sticky banner: '30-Day Energy Guarantee — Feel sharper or 100% refund. No questions asked.' Below price, add: '₹33/day — less than your evening chai. Cancel anytime.' Add subtle scarcity: '847 packs sold this week' (if true). This eliminates risk perception and reframes price as daily investment.
Visual Design → Lifestyle Shots 4.0
Zero lifestyle imagery showing Tejas's world — no gym scenes, no work meetings, no travel context, no evening family time. All images are product shots, ingredient flatlays, clinical/lab imagery, or headshot testimonials. Model consuming gummy is in neutral studio setting.
Add 3 lifestyle shots: (1) Professional in business casual, focused in a late afternoon meeting while others look tired, (2) Same man at gym after work with visible energy, (3) Evening scene — active with family, not collapsed on couch. Show gummy bottle on office desk and in gym bag. Make Tejas think: 'That's my day. This is for me.'
Reviews → Freshness 5.0
All 5 reviews are from late April to early May 2026 (106-117 days old). No reviews from June-August 2026. Review velocity stopped completely after May 10th.
Implement automated post-purchase email at Day 14: 'Hi [Name], you've been taking Shilajit for 2 weeks — feeling the difference? Share your experience and get ₹100 off your next order.' Target customers from June-August 2026 with a one-time review request campaign. Aim for 2-3 new reviews per week minimum.
Persona × Narrative → CTA Language 5.0
CTAs are generic: 'Add to Cart' and 'Buy Now'. For Tejas, who needs peer/trainer recommendation or trust signals to purchase, the CTA feels transactional rather than reassuring.
Replace 'Add to Cart' with 'Start My 30-Day Energy Reset' (primary) and 'Buy Now' with 'Try Risk-Free Today'. Add micro-copy directly below CTA: '✓ 30-day guarantee ✓ Cancel anytime ✓ 12,000+ men switched'. This transforms the CTA from transaction to commitment with safety net.
Persona × Narrative → Hero / Banner 5.5
Headline 'Shilajit Gummies (1 Month Pack)' is product-centric, not problem-centric. Subhead 'Daily Energy for Working Men' is better aligned but buried below the fold.
Rewrite hero headline to: 'Stay Sharp from 10 AM to 7 PM — Without the Crash'. Subhead: 'The Daily Energy Gummy Built for Working Men Like You'. Move 'Shilajit Gummies' to smaller product descriptor text. Lead with his pain, not your ingredient.

Human Presence
6.5/10
Human presence appears in only 3 contexts: Image 2 shows a young, fit Indian male (late 20s-early 30s) consuming the gummy with a calm, confident expression. Testimonial images (22-26) show real male users aged 29-39 with professions listed (Business, IT, Pharma). Factory tour banner shows workers in pink lab coats. However, no lifestyle imagery shows Tejas's actual context - a busy professional balancing gym, travel, and work fatigue. The model in Image 2 appears younger and more relaxed than the persona's stressed, mid-career reality.
Add 1-2 lifestyle shots showing a 35-40 year old professional experiencing the 3 PM crash at a desk or in a meeting, then a contrasting shot of sustained energy during evening family time or gym session. Match the testimonial age range more closely to the persona (35-45).
Proof Prominence
8.0/10
Clinical proof is well-represented: Image 7 prominently displays '25%' and '23%' stats in large typography with the gummy as visual anchor. '2.5x better absorbed' claim appears in Image 5 with gut illustration. Image 6 shows batch testing setup with quality metrics visible. Benefits carousel (17-21) walks through clinical study methodology with numbered steps. Journal names appear in Image 21. However, the 25%/23% numbers in Image 7 lack immediate context - 'Fitness Score' requires explanation.
Add a parenthetical '(VO₂ max)' directly beside 'Fitness Score' in Image 7. Consider making the journal logos more prominent in the clinical claims slide rather than just text names. Add a trust badge or certification seal near proof elements.
Ingredient Imagery
7.5/10
Image 3 shows four key ingredients (Shilajit, KSM-66 Ashwagandha, Black Muesli, Chicory Root) in glass petri dishes against a clean backdrop - scientific and premium presentation. Individual ingredient slides (11-14) repeat this with benefit statements. Shilajit appears as a dark mineral chunk, Ashwagandha as dried root sticks. However, the imagery is functional rather than aspirational - ingredients look clinical/educational rather than premium/desirable. Black Musli appears as small pellets that could be mistaken for anything.
Upgrade ingredient photography with warmer lighting and subtle shadows to make them look more premium. Add origin story elements (Himalayan backdrop for Shilajit, farm imagery for Ashwagandha). Before / After
5.5/10
No explicit before/after visual exists. The problem slide (Image 10) explains the crash scientifically but doesn't show a person experiencing it. Testimonials describe transformations verbally but lack visual proof.
Create a split-frame visual showing the same professional at 3 PM: left side depleted at desk with coffee cups, right side alert and focused. Or show morning-to-evening energy timeline with visual energy indicators. Consider adding user-submitted before/after energy diary screenshots.

Strong brand consistency: warm beige/cream backgrounds throughout, 'Man Matters' logo placement is consistent, black/gold/cream color palette maintained. Visual Design → Before / After 3.0
Image 3 shows user testimonial benefits as text callouts ('No afternoon crash', 'Energy levels are back', 'Stress feels more manageable') but no visual transformation. Clinical stats (25% fitness, 23% cortisol) are presented as data without human representation.
Create a 'Day 1 vs Day 90' split-frame featuring a relatable 30-something professional: left side shows slumped posture at laptop with coffee cups, right side shows same man alert in standing meeting. Overlay the clinical stats on the transformation image to anchor data to human outcome.
Ad Alignment → ATC Drop-off Addressed 3.5
ATC rates in ads are 13-30%, but PDP has no urgency triggers, no risk-reversal, 'Summer ready' headline is seasonal/weak, and FAQ section 'teased but not shown — forces clicks away.'
Add directly above ATC: '60-Day Energy Guarantee — Feel the difference or full refund. No questions.' Replace 'Summer ready' with 'All-day energy in 2 gummies. No prep. No excuses.' Expand FAQ inline on PDP—eliminate the click-away. Add strikethrough pricing showing original vs current price.
Reviews → Negative Handling 4.0
No negative reviews displayed. Review #3 hints at resolved objection ('bad taste' of traditional shilajit). Review #5 mentions 'initial skepticism' but no actual criticism. Zero brand responses visible.
Surface one authentic 3-4 star review mentioning 'takes 3 months for results' (already noted in reviews #3, #5) with a brand response: 'Thanks for your patience, [Name]. Most customers feel sustained energy by week 6—we recommend the 3-month supply for best results. Reach out anytime.' This converts an objection into expectation-setting.
Visual Design → Lifestyle Shots 4.0
No images show gym, office, or travel contexts. Product appears in 'abstract studio settings (blue sky backdrop, neutral surfaces).' Testimonial images are 'static portraits, not in-context lifestyle moments.'
Add three contextual shots: (1) Open gym bag with gummy jar next to protein shaker and AirPods, (2) Minimalist desk setup with gummy jar beside laptop at 3pm timestamp, (3) Airplane tray table with gummy jar and passport. Each image should feel like Tejas's Instagram feed, not a catalog.
Persona × Narrative → CTA Language 4.5
'Add to Cart | Buy Now' is the current CTA. No acknowledgment of Tejas's objection around 'no trainer or trusted peer recommendation.' Missing social proof integration at decision point.
Replace CTA with: 'Start Your 30-Day Energy Reset' with micro-copy beneath: 'Join 50,000+ men who ditched the messy resin.' Add a single line of rotating testimonial snippets above CTA: '"Finally, something that fits my schedule" — Verified Buyer, Mumbai'
Reviews → Freshness 5.0
All 5 reviews are from late May 2026 (87-97 days ago), clustering within 10 days of each other. No reviews from June, July, or August 2026. Pattern suggests 'campaign or incentivized review burst rather than organic accumulation.'
Implement automated post-purchase email at Day 21 and Day 45 requesting reviews. Incentivize with 'Review & get 15% off your next order.' Target 2-3 new reviews monthly. Display review dates prominently to showcase recency—'Reviewed 3 days ago' creates urgency and authenticity.
